decks.name: How Tall
decks.tagline: A tennis net to the top of Everest
decks.axis: Shortest at the top, tallest at the bottom.

cards.label: A tennis net at the posts
cards.note: Three and a half feet at the posts, three feet in the middle — it sags on purpose.

cards.label: A dromedary camel at the hump
cards.note: The hump is fat, not water. It shrinks and flops over when the camel is running on empty.

cards.label: A football goal crossbar
cards.note: Eight feet exactly, unchanged since 1863.

cards.label: An ostrich
cards.note: The tallest bird alive, and the only one with two toes.

cards.label: A high-cube shipping container
cards.note: Nine feet six inches. The standard box is a foot shorter.

cards.label: A basketball hoop
cards.note: Ten feet, chosen in 1891 because that was the height of the gym's balcony rail.

cards.label: An African elephant at the shoulder
cards.note: Shoulder height — the trunk raised adds another two metres or so.

cards.label: A Routemaster double-decker bus
cards.note: Low bridges across Britain are signed for exactly this reason.

cards.label: A giraffe
cards.note: Its neck has seven vertebrae — the same number as yours.

cards.label: The tallest sunflower ever grown
cards.note: Grown by Hans-Peter Schiffer in Germany, 2014. He holds the record three times over.

cards.label: An Olympic diving platform
cards.note: You hit the water at about 55 km/h, roughly 1.4 seconds later.

cards.label: A letter of the Hollywood Sign
cards.note: It originally read HOLLYWOODLAND and was meant to last eighteen months.

cards.label: The Angel of the North
cards.note: Its wingspan is wider than it is tall — 54 metres, near enough a jumbo jet.

cards.label: Christ the Redeemer, statue only
cards.note: The pedestal adds another eight metres. It is struck by lightning several times a year.

cards.label: The Statue of Liberty, heel to head
cards.note: Torch to pedestal base is 46 m; the whole monument from the ground is 93 m.

cards.label: The Colosseum
cards.note: Four storeys, and it could be emptied of 50,000 people in minutes.

cards.label: Niagara's Horseshoe Falls
cards.note: Not especially tall — its fame is the width and the volume, not the drop.

cards.label: The Leaning Tower of Pisa
cards.note: Measured on the low side; the high side is about 56.7 m. It started leaning during construction.

cards.label: The tallest shell of the Sydney Opera House
cards.note: The shells are all cut from the surface of one imaginary sphere.

cards.label: General Sherman, the largest tree on Earth
cards.note: Not the tallest — the largest by volume. It has been growing for over 2,000 years.

cards.label: The Elizabeth Tower, home of Big Ben
cards.note: Big Ben is the bell inside, not the tower.

cards.label: Victoria Falls
cards.note: The locals call it Mosi-oa-Tunya — the smoke that thunders.

cards.label: Hyperion, the tallest tree on Earth
cards.note: A coast redwood in California. Its location is kept secret to protect it.

cards.label: The Great Pyramid of Giza today
cards.note: It was 146.6 m when finished, and the tallest thing humans had built for 3,800 years.

cards.label: Blackpool Tower
cards.note: Built in 1894 as a half-scale answer to the Eiffel Tower.

cards.label: The Washington Monument
cards.note: The stone changes colour a third of the way up, where construction stopped for 23 years.

cards.label: The Statue of Unity
cards.note: In Gujarat, India — the tallest statue in the world, twice the height of the Statue of Liberty.

cards.label: The Gateway Arch in St Louis
cards.note: It is exactly as wide at the base as it is tall.

cards.label: The Golden Gate Bridge towers
cards.note: Measured above the water. The colour is called International Orange.

cards.label: The Shard
cards.note: The tallest building in the UK, and deliberately never finished at the top — the shards are left open.

cards.label: The Eiffel Tower to the tip
cards.note: It grows about 15 cm on a hot day as the iron expands.

cards.label: The Empire State Building to the tip
cards.note: The roof is at 381 m; the spire was built as a mooring mast for airships.

cards.label: The Petronas Towers
cards.note: The world's tallest building for six years, and still the tallest twin towers.

cards.label: One World Trade Center
cards.note: 1,776 feet, for the year of American independence.

cards.label: The CN Tower
cards.note: The world's tallest free-standing structure for 32 years.

cards.label: The Tokyo Skytree
cards.note: 634 was chosen because it can be read in Japanese as mu-sa-shi, the region's old name.

cards.label: Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur
cards.note: The second-tallest building on Earth, finished in 2023.

cards.label: The Burj Khalifa
cards.note: The lifts travel at 10 metres per second and it still takes about a minute to the top.

cards.label: Angel Falls
cards.note: So tall the water atomises into mist before it lands.

cards.label: Table Mountain
cards.note: Its flat top is roughly 3 km across.

cards.label: Mount Vesuvius
cards.note: It was far taller before 79 AD — the eruption took the top off.

cards.label: Ben Nevis
cards.note: The highest point in the British Isles, and it was once a volcano.

cards.label: Mount Kosciuszko
cards.note: The highest point in mainland Australia — you can walk up it in an afternoon.

cards.label: Mount Olympus
cards.note: Home of the Greek gods, and not climbed by a human until 1913.

cards.label: Mount Fuji
cards.note: Still an active volcano. It last erupted in 1707.

cards.label: The Matterhorn
cards.note: Four faces, each pointing almost exactly at a compass point.

cards.label: Mont Blanc
cards.note: The summit is a dome of ice, so the official height changes by a metre or two each survey.

cards.label: Kilimanjaro
cards.note: The tallest free-standing mountain on Earth — it rises straight off the plain.

cards.label: Denali
cards.note: Measured from its base it is a bigger climb than Everest.

cards.label: Aconcagua
cards.note: The highest peak outside Asia, and you can reach the top without ropes.

cards.label: K2
cards.note: Lower than Everest and far deadlier. Nobody had climbed it in winter until 2021.

cards.label: Mount Everest
cards.note: Re-measured jointly by Nepal and China in 2020, settling a long argument.

cards.label: Mauna Kea from its base on the seafloor
cards.note: Measured from the ocean floor it beats Everest comfortably. Only 4,207 m of it is above water.

cards.label: An airliner at cruising altitude
cards.note: About 36,000 feet — high enough that the air outside is around −55°C.

decks.name: How Fast
decks.tagline: A garden snail to the speed of light
decks.axis: Slowest at the top, fastest at the bottom.

cards.label: A garden snail
cards.note: About a millimetre and a half per second. A marathon would take it around three weeks.

cards.label: A three-toed sloth on the ground
cards.note: It is roughly three times quicker in the trees, which is where it would rather be.

cards.label: A person walking
cards.note: The speed most pedestrian crossings are timed for.

cards.label: A house fly
cards.note: Slow, but it can change direction in 30 thousandths of a second.

cards.label: The fastest competitive swimmer
cards.note: Peak speed over 50 m freestyle. Water is roughly 800 times denser than air.

cards.label: A domestic pig
cards.note: Faster than most people expect, and faster than most people.

cards.label: A black mamba
cards.note: The fastest snake on Earth — and it does that with no legs.

cards.label: A honeybee
cards.note: Its wings beat about 230 times a second to manage it.

cards.label: A blue whale at a sprint
cards.note: Not bad for the largest animal that has ever lived.

cards.label: Usain Bolt at his fastest
cards.note: Measured between 60 and 80 m of his 9.58 world record. He was still accelerating at 60 m.

cards.label: A domestic cat
cards.note: Faster than the fastest human sprinter, over a short distance.

cards.label: A killer whale
cards.note: The fastest marine mammal, and it hunts in coordinated packs.

cards.label: An ostrich
cards.note: The fastest animal on two legs. Its stride is over three metres.

cards.label: A greyhound
cards.note: Second only to the cheetah on land, and it can hold the pace far longer.

cards.label: A hummingbird in its courtship dive
cards.note: Relative to its size, that is faster than a fighter jet on afterburner.

cards.label: A cheetah
cards.note: It can only hold that for about 30 seconds before it overheats.

cards.label: The fastest skateboard ever ridden
cards.note: Kyle Wester, downhill in Colorado, 2017. Standing up.

cards.label: The fastest cricket delivery ever bowled
cards.note: Shoaib Akhtar to Nick Knight, 2003. The batter has about 0.4 seconds to react.

cards.label: The fastest baseball pitch ever thrown
cards.note: Aroldis Chapman, 2010 — 105.1 mph.

cards.label: A skydiver in freefall
cards.note: Terminal velocity belly-to-earth. Head-down it is closer to 300.

cards.label: Formula Rossa, the fastest rollercoaster
cards.note: Riders wear goggles, because at that speed an insect to the eye is a serious injury.

cards.label: The wind in a Category 5 hurricane
cards.note: That is the minimum for Category 5. There is no Category 6.

cards.label: The fastest tennis serve ever recorded
cards.note: Sam Groth, Busan, 2012 — in a tournament that did not count for ATP records.

cards.label: The fastest bicycle ever ridden
cards.note: Denise Mueller-Korenek, 2018, drafting behind a dragster on the Bonneville Salt Flats.

cards.label: A Shinkansen in normal service
cards.note: In nearly 60 years of operation it has never had a passenger fatality from a derailment or collision.

cards.label: A Formula 1 car at its fastest
cards.note: Valtteri Bottas, Mexico, 2016 — thin air at altitude helps.

cards.label: A peregrine falcon in a dive
cards.note: The fastest animal on Earth. It has baffles in its nostrils so the airflow does not burst its lungs.

cards.label: The strongest wind gust ever recorded
cards.note: Barrow Island, Australia, during Cyclone Olivia in 1996.

cards.label: The Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+
cards.note: The first production car past 300 mph, on VW's own test track.

cards.label: The fastest badminton smash ever recorded
cards.note: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, 2023. The shuttle decelerates violently — it is nothing like that when it arrives.

cards.label: The world rail speed record
cards.note: A modified TGV in 2007, on conventional rails.

cards.label: The world maglev speed record
cards.note: Japan's L0 series, 2015 — floating, so no rails to touch.

cards.label: A Boeing 747 at cruise
cards.note: About Mach 0.85. Above that the wings start making their own shockwaves.

cards.label: The speed of sound at sea level
cards.note: It falls as air gets colder — which is why supersonic records are set high or in the desert.

cards.label: Felix Baumgartner's freefall
cards.note: In 2012 he became the first human to go supersonic without a vehicle.

cards.label: The Earth's surface at the equator
cards.note: You are doing this right now, sitting still.

cards.label: Concorde at cruise
cards.note: Mach 2.04. The airframe grew about 25 cm in flight from the heat.

cards.label: The SR-71 Blackbird's record
cards.note: It leaked fuel on the ground — the panels only sealed once heat expanded them in flight.

cards.label: The International Space Station in orbit
cards.note: A sunrise every 90 minutes.

cards.label: Apollo 10 on re-entry
cards.note: Still the fastest any human being has ever travelled.

cards.label: Voyager 1 leaving the Solar System
cards.note: Launched in 1977 and still sending data back.

cards.label: The Earth orbiting the Sun
cards.note: Also happening right now, also while you sit still.

cards.label: The Parker Solar Probe at closest approach
cards.note: The fastest object humans have ever built, whipped around by the Sun's gravity.

cards.label: Light
cards.note: Exactly 299,792,458 metres per second — the metre is defined from it, so the number cannot change.

decks.name: How Long Ago
decks.tagline: Magna Carta to a nudged asteroid
decks.axis: Oldest at the top, most recent at the bottom.

cards.label: The University of Bologna is founded
cards.note: The oldest university in continuous operation anywhere in the world.

cards.label: Magna Carta is sealed
cards.note: King John repudiated it within ten weeks. Three of its clauses are still law in England.

cards.label: Gutenberg's printing press
cards.note: The date is approximate — his Bible was finished around 1455.

cards.label: Columbus reaches the Americas
cards.note: He died still insisting he had reached Asia.

cards.label: Shakespeare is born
cards.note: The baptism is recorded on 26 April; the birthday is a guess.

cards.label: The telescope
cards.note: Hans Lippershey filed for the patent. Galileo heard about it and built his own within months.

cards.label: Newton publishes the Principia
cards.note: Halley paid for the printing out of his own pocket.

cards.label: Watt patents his improved steam engine
cards.note: The separate condenser — it did not invent the steam engine, it made it worth running.

cards.label: The first crewed hot-air balloon flight
cards.note: The Montgolfiers sent up a sheep, a duck and a rooster first.

cards.label: The first steam locomotive runs on rails
cards.note: Trevithick's engine at Penydarren. It broke the cast-iron rails.

cards.label: The stethoscope
cards.note: Laennec rolled up paper because he was too embarrassed to put his ear to a woman's chest.

cards.label: The oldest surviving photograph
cards.note: Niépce's view from a window. The exposure took several hours.

cards.label: The electric telegraph
cards.note: Cooke and Wheatstone's patent. Within twenty years a cable crossed the Atlantic.

cards.label: On the Origin of Species
cards.note: Darwin sat on the idea for twenty years and only published when someone else got close.

cards.label: The London Underground opens
cards.note: The first trains were steam. Underground.

cards.label: The periodic table
cards.note: Mendeleev left gaps and predicted what would fill them. He was right.

cards.label: Bell patents the telephone
cards.note: Elisha Gray filed a competing claim the same day. The argument never really ended.

cards.label: Edison's practical light bulb
cards.note: He did not invent the bulb — he found a filament that lasted.

cards.label: The Benz Patent-Motorwagen
cards.note: Bertha Benz took it on the first long drive two years later without telling her husband.

cards.label: The pneumatic tyre
cards.note: Dunlop made it for his son's tricycle.

cards.label: Basketball is invented
cards.note: James Naismith nailed up two peach baskets. Someone had to fetch the ball down after every score.

cards.label: Röntgen discovers X-rays
cards.note: The first X-ray image was of his wife's hand. She said she had seen her own death.

cards.label: The first modern Olympic Games
cards.note: Athens, 14 nations, 241 athletes, all of them men.

cards.label: The first transatlantic radio signal
cards.note: Marconi sent the letter S. Physicists had said the curve of the Earth made it impossible.

cards.label: The Wright brothers fly
cards.note: The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered less than the wingspan of a 747.

cards.label: Bakelite, the first synthetic plastic
cards.note: Made from nothing that had ever been alive — that was the genuinely new part.

cards.label: Ford's moving assembly line
cards.note: It cut the build time of a Model T from twelve hours to about ninety minutes.

cards.label: The first television demonstration
cards.note: Baird's picture was 30 lines. The subject was a ventriloquist's dummy.

cards.label: Penicillin is discovered
cards.note: Fleming found it by leaving a plate out over a holiday. It took another 14 years to make it a drug.

cards.label: The jet engine is patented
cards.note: Frank Whittle, aged 22. The Air Ministry was not interested.

cards.label: Nylon
cards.note: The first stockings sold out in a day and were rationed within four years for parachutes.

cards.label: The supermarket trolley
cards.note: Sylvan Goldman had to hire actors to push them around before anyone would use one.

cards.label: The ballpoint pen is patented
cards.note: László Bíró was a newspaper editor who noticed printing ink dried faster.

cards.label: The microwave oven
cards.note: Percy Spencer noticed a chocolate bar melting in his pocket beside a radar set.

cards.label: The transistor
cards.note: Bell Labs. Everything with a chip in it descends from this.

cards.label: The Polaroid instant camera goes on sale
cards.note: Edwin Land's daughter asked why she could not see the photo straight away.

cards.label: The structure of DNA
cards.note: Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images, shown to Watson and Crick without her knowledge.

cards.label: Sputnik
cards.note: A polished metal sphere the size of a beach ball, beeping. It terrified Washington.

cards.label: The Lego brick is patented
cards.note: A brick made that year still clutches one made today.

cards.label: The first human in space
cards.note: Gagarin's flight lasted 108 minutes and he ejected before landing.

cards.label: The Moon landing
cards.note: The guidance computer had about 4 kilobytes of memory.

cards.label: The microprocessor
cards.note: Intel's 4004 — a whole CPU on one chip, built for a desk calculator.

cards.label: The first handheld mobile phone call
cards.note: Martin Cooper rang his rival at Bell Labs to tell him he had lost.

cards.label: Voyager 1 launches
cards.note: It carries a gold record of Earth sounds, aimed at nobody in particular.

cards.label: The Sony Walkman
cards.note: Sony's own engineers thought a tape player that could not record would never sell.

cards.label: The IBM PC
cards.note: IBM licensed the operating system rather than buying it. That decision made Microsoft.

cards.label: The internet switches to TCP/IP
cards.note: 1 January. This is the closest thing the internet has to a birthday.

cards.label: Super Mario Bros.
cards.note: The clouds and the bushes are the same sprite in different colours — memory was that tight.

cards.label: The World Wide Web is proposed
cards.note: Berners-Lee's boss wrote 'vague but exciting' on the memo.

cards.label: Linux
cards.note: Announced as 'just a hobby, won't be big and professional'.

cards.label: Toy Story
cards.note: The first feature film made entirely with computer graphics.

cards.label: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
cards.note: He accused it of cheating. The suspicious move was later traced to a bug.

cards.label: Google is founded
cards.note: They tried to sell it for a million dollars the following year. The buyer haggled.

cards.label: The iPod
cards.note: A thousand songs in your pocket, and a hard drive that did not like being dropped.

cards.label: Facebook launches
cards.note: Harvard only, and you needed a university email address.

cards.label: YouTube
cards.note: The first video is 19 seconds of a co-founder at the zoo.

cards.label: The first iPhone
cards.note: It could not record video, send a picture message, or run an app you had not been given.

cards.label: Instagram
cards.note: Square photos, because that was the shape of a Polaroid.

cards.label: The Higgs boson is confirmed
cards.note: Predicted in 1964. It took 48 years and a 27-km ring to find it.

cards.label: Gravitational waves are announced
cards.note: Two black holes colliding stretched a 4-km detector by less than the width of a proton.

cards.label: The first photograph of a black hole
cards.note: Eight radio telescopes across the planet, working as one dish the size of Earth.

cards.label: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
cards.note: It had 344 single points of failure to unfold. All of them worked.

cards.label: DART deflects an asteroid
cards.note: The first time humans have deliberately changed the orbit of another world.

decks.name: How Heavy
decks.tagline: A tennis ball to the Great Pyramid
decks.axis: Lightest at the top, heaviest at the bottom.

cards.label: A tennis ball
cards.note: It also has to bounce to a specified height when dropped from 254 cm.

cards.label: A cricket ball
cards.note: Between 155.9 g and 163 g — the rules specify it to a tenth of a gram.

cards.label: An iPhone 15
cards.note: Aluminium frame. The Pro is titanium and slightly heavier.

cards.label: A size-5 football
cards.note: Weighed dry. A leather ball in the rain used to gain half a kilo.

cards.label: A basketball
cards.note: Size 7, the men's ball. The women's ball is about 60 g lighter.

cards.label: A litre of water
cards.note: Not a coincidence — the kilogram was originally defined this way.

cards.label: An adult human brain
cards.note: Two per cent of your body weight and twenty per cent of your energy budget.

cards.label: A newborn baby
cards.note: The world average at birth.

cards.label: A house cat
cards.note: Roughly. Your cat may dispute the figure.

cards.label: A racing bicycle at the legal minimum
cards.note: Cycling's governing body sets a floor so bikes do not become dangerously flimsy.

cards.label: A bowling ball at the maximum legal weight
cards.note: Sixteen pounds — exactly the same as a men's shot put.

cards.label: A beagle
cards.note: Bred to be small enough to follow on foot rather than on horseback.

cards.label: A Good Delivery gold bar
cards.note: The bar central banks trade. One is worth roughly a million dollars.

cards.label: A border collie
cards.note: One named Chaser learned the names of 1,022 objects.

cards.label: A bag of cement
cards.note: The standard European sack. It used to be 50 kg until backs were considered.

cards.label: An emperor penguin
cards.note: The male fasts for over two months on the ice while incubating the egg.

cards.label: A labrador
cards.note: The most popular dog breed in the world for three decades running.

cards.label: A grey wolf
cards.note: Every dog on this list is descended from one.

cards.label: A cheetah
cards.note: Light on purpose — the whole animal is built as a sprinting frame.

cards.label: An adult human, world average
cards.note: The global mean across all adults. It varies enormously by region.

cards.label: A giant panda
cards.note: It eats up to 14 hours a day because bamboo barely feeds it.

cards.label: An adult male gorilla
cards.note: Almost entirely vegetarian.

cards.label: A male lion
cards.note: The mane is not armour — it advertises condition.

cards.label: A Siberian tiger
cards.note: The largest cat alive.

cards.label: A male grizzly bear
cards.note: It can double that before hibernation.

cards.label: A polar bear
cards.note: Its skin is black and its fur is hollow and colourless, not white.

cards.label: A concert grand piano
cards.note: There are around 20 tonnes of tension across the strings inside it.

cards.label: A racehorse
cards.note: Carrying a jockey who is required to weigh about a tenth of that.

cards.label: A Ford Model T
cards.note: Fifteen million were built. A modern hatchback is more than twice as heavy.

cards.label: A cubic metre of water
cards.note: One tonne exactly, by the original definition. Water is unhelpfully heavy.

cards.label: A great white shark
cards.note: It has never been kept successfully in an aquarium for long.

cards.label: A giraffe
cards.note: Its heart alone weighs about 11 kg, to push blood two metres uphill.

cards.label: A hippopotamus
cards.note: It cannot actually swim — it walks along the bottom.

cards.label: A white rhinoceros
cards.note: The horn is keratin, the same material as your fingernails.

cards.label: An African bush elephant
cards.note: The largest land animal alive.

cards.label: A Routemaster double-decker bus
cards.note: Unladen. It was built with aluminium to keep it this light.

cards.label: A Tyrannosaurus rex
cards.note: A best estimate from skeletons — the range runs from about 6 to 9 tonnes.

cards.label: A blue whale
cards.note: The heaviest animal that has ever lived, as far as anyone knows.

cards.label: The Statue of Liberty
cards.note: The copper skin is only 2.4 mm thick — about two pennies.

cards.label: A fully loaded Boeing 747-400
cards.note: Maximum take-off weight. Nearly half of it can be fuel.

cards.label: The Space Shuttle at launch
cards.note: Most of that is the external tank, which was thrown away every flight.

cards.label: A Saturn V at launch
cards.note: The heaviest and most powerful rocket ever flown successfully.

cards.label: The iron in the Eiffel Tower
cards.note: Melted down it would fill its own base to a depth of about 6 cm.

cards.label: The Titanic
cards.note: Displacement, fully loaded. Modern cruise ships are four times heavier.

cards.label: A Nimitz-class aircraft carrier
cards.note: It carries two nuclear reactors and never needs refuelling for 20 years.

cards.label: The Golden Gate Bridge
cards.note: The main span hangs from two cables, each spun from 27,572 individual wires.

cards.label: The Great Pyramid of Giza
cards.note: About 2.3 million blocks, and it stayed the heaviest building on Earth for millennia.
